item.title: Mini Crackme
item.description: Target: Windows x86-64, single argument passed in ecx. check: mov eax, ecx / xor eax, 3Ch / ror eax, 3 / cmp eax, 7 / jne fail / mov eax, 1 / ret / fail: mov eax, 0 / ret -- ror eax, 3 rotates all 32 bits of eax right by 3 positions, wrapping bits off the low end into the high end. Find the decimal value (0-255) passed in ecx that makes check return 1. --- Answer: 4. Explanation: 1) Work backwards from the compare: eax must equal 7 after the rotate, so before the rotate it must equal rol(7, 3) -- rotating 0x00000007 left by 3 gives 0x00000038. 2) That 0x38 is the value of eax right after the xor, so ecx = 0x38 XOR 0x3C = 0x04. 3) ecx = 4 decimal; XOR and rotate are both one-to-one on 32-bit values, so this is the unique byte satisfying the check.
